thread:
alex: Morning async — quick standup. What I did: pushed routing policy changes to canary for customer-rate-limit. Verified new path rewriting worked for /v1/ingest. Blockers: seeing 429 spikes in the canary metrics around burst windows; unclear if it's the client or our burst config. Today: will dig into throttle logs and add a tighter bucket for short bursts. pinging @maria for the quota knobs.
maria: saw the 429s too. I checked the rate-policy manifest and the burst window looks correct. Could be the edge returning 429s pre-ratelimit because of JWT validation latency. I’ll check auth latency traces.
tyler: fyi I merged a small fix to kv-cache eviction that reduces mem churn (PR: https://git.redwood/infer/pulls/342). Not related to 429s but reduces noisy GC during high QPS.
sam: quick heads-up — I deployed a patch to the api-gw that changes the default fallback-model route; might affect routing weights if a variant is missing. Rollback ready if we see issues. Deploy-bot: canary started at 09:12 UTC (deploy id: d-2026-09). Status: healthy.
alex: thanks. @sam — can you confirm that fallback changes don't touch the rate-limiter order? We want rate checks before model fallback.
sam: they don't. order preserved: auth -> rate_limit -> routing -> fallback. I added a unit test but will add an integration smoke tomorrow.
nina: blocker on my side: trying to run local canary for the new rate policy, but my docker image keeps hitting DockerHub rate limits during CI. Anyone able to share a cached image or a different registry? :sweat_smile:
maria: use our internal registry: registry.redwood.local/infra/gateway:canary-2026-09. It has the auth binary with tracing enabled. @nina: LMK if you can't access.
nina: got it, thanks — pulling now.
tyler: small question for reviewers: I left a comment on PR 347 about the retry backoff in the auth client. Changing to jittered exponential seems low risk but want prod opinion.
alex: @tyler — +1 to jittered backoff. Also please add a config flag so we can toggle without redeploy.
sam: there’s one perf nuance: jitter increases tail variability, but for auth calls it's fine. Add flag and default to on for now.
maria: update: auth traces show a spike at 09:05 UTC correlated with a batch of long JWT verifications from an old client library. Suggest we add a short-circuit cache for validated tokens for 30s to absorb bursts.
alex: good call. Can you draft the cache change and a short safety TTL so it expires if keys rotate? Keep it configurable (env var).
maria: will do. I’ll open a draft PR and link here when ready.
sam: one more thing — routing policy lint job flagged a rule with overlapping matchers (/v1/ingest vs /v1/ingest-beta). We should prioritize exact match over prefix; I'll push a fix to the linter.
tyler: nice. That explains a few misrouted requests I saw yesterday.
alex: blockers summary: 429 spikes (investigating), nina had registry access issue (resolved), confirm retries/backoff config. Actions: maria to open token-cache PR, sam to patch linter and keep an eye on canary, tyler to add flag to backoff change, alex will look at throttle logs and correlate with edge 429s. If anyone wants pairing, I'm available in #eng-platform huddles.
deploy-bot: Canary monitoring alert: 5xx rate within acceptable SLO, 429 increased by +3.1% in last 10m. Escalation not triggered.
maria: linked draft PR: https://git.redwood/infer/pulls/351 — token-cache (TTL configurable). Please review when you have a sec.
alex: great. If we don't see improvements in the next 30m, we’ll roll the canary back. Otherwise we can promote the policy and merge the token cache. Thanks team :thumbsup:
